`r lectureLine(6)`

Some things are, I think, nicely going to come together, because we're going to be talking about how to do a correlation analysis, and we go from variance and covariance to r. How do we get actually a significance for a correlation value? To get the p for r, we need to go to t, so we pay a visit to the t-distribution, the sampling distribution of various observed statistics. And then we'll take a look at what it means to do a partial correlation, a first look at how you can work with multiple predictor variables, and at the end, I will let JASP do the heavy lifting for you.

Open the recording and skip to the chapter you need. The chapters come from the lecture transcript, so one may start a few seconds early or late.
